archetype.name: Pocket Passer (big-arm, mobile when forced)
archetype.definition: A tall, strong-armed thrower built to work from the pocket and attack downfield. He has run more when protection breaks, including 498 rushing yards last season, but his value still comes from what he does as a passer.

report.headline: A broken line and a broken downfield game, not a broken quarterback.
report.take:
Herbert has spent six seasons as a steady above-average starter. His EPA per play has stayed positive every year, from 0.065 to 0.199. He has ranked inside the top 25 in that stat each season, with positive CPOE in four of the last five years. The 2026 version is posting -0.157 EPA per dropback (35th of 42), -4.35 CPOE and six interceptions in four games, all of them losses. A drop that steep from a quarterback with that track record needs a cause. The dossier offers a clear one in the protection and in where the ball is going.

The Chargers rank 32nd of 32 in offensive hit rate, and Herbert has been hit or sacked on 22.9% of dropbacks. His pressure-to-sack rate (25.8%) is middle of the pack and in line with the 30%-plus he carried in 2024 and 2025, so he isn't holding the ball into sacks any more than usual. The 9.2% sack rate comes from how often he is under fire.

The damage shows up in the depth splits:
- Behind the line and short of 10 yards, he is fine: +0.244 and +0.124 EPA on 69 attempts, with no interceptions.
- At 10 or more air yards, he is 21 of 50 (42%), with all six interceptions.
- On throws of 20-plus yards, he is 5 of 17 with a -10.4 CPOE.

That is what it looks like when a quarterback has to let it go before the route has developed.

Game state has made it worse. Within one score he is at -0.268 EPA with nine of his 12 sacks. In close fourth quarters he is at -1.028 over 17 plays, with five sacks. When the game was already lopsided against him, his efficiency was close to neutral. The pattern points to pressure in obvious passing situations, a third-down average of 8.8 yards to go, and a Harbaugh offense that passes 9 points below expectation and leaves him in long-yardage spots.

The opponents explain little. He was just as poor against Arizona and Buffalo, now 27th and 29th in defensive EPA, as against Seattle, and his least-negative game came against Las Vegas, now ranked second.

What the numbers hide is that the efficient part of his game is still intact. The red zone has been sharp: 4 touchdowns on 13 attempts, no interceptions and a +19.2 CPOE. Ladd McConkey (+0.629 EPA per target) and Tre Harris (+0.28) are producing.

The trouble is that the line is getting worse before it gets better:
- Rashawn Slater is out 4-to-6 weeks with a high-ankle sprain.
- Joe Alt left Week 4 with a neck injury and is questionable.
- Both guards, Awosika and Penning, are banged up.
- McConkey is week-to-week with a foot injury.

The interception rate should come down, since 5% is far above even his worst career seasons. Getting back to his normal level, though, depends on protection he may not have for a month.

strengths.title: The quick game still works
strengths.body: Throws behind the line and in the 0-9 range have been positive and turnover-free. That is the part of the offense that doesn't depend on protection holding. It is a skill he has always had and a reliable fallback while the tackles are hurt.

strengths.title: Sharp inside the 20
strengths.body: All four of his touchdowns came in the red zone, with no interceptions and a completion rate far above expected. On 13 attempts that rate won't hold, but the compressed field takes away the long-developing throws that are hurting him elsewhere.

strengths.title: A long record of competent play
strengths.body: He has posted positive EPA per play in all six prior seasons, including +0.167 in 2024 and +0.09 in 2025. A four-game crash during a stretch of severe line injuries is more likely circumstance than decline. His bad-throw rate (12.6%) is right in line with his career.

concerns.title: Protection is the worst in football
concerns.body: The Chargers rank last in offensive hit rate, and Slater is now out until roughly November. Alt and both guards also carry injury tags. This is not a flaw in Herbert's game, but it is the cause of most of the rest, and it gets worse before it improves.

concerns.title: Every interception came downfield
concerns.body: All six interceptions came on throws of 10-plus air yards, and his deep completion rate is 29.4%. Some of that is pressure forcing early, off-platform throws. He has also had 13- and 15-interception seasons, so the downfield risk-taking is partly who he is. Expect fewer interceptions, but not a clean sheet.

concerns.title: Close games fall apart late
concerns.body: In one-score games he has been well below average, and in close fourth quarters he is losing a point per play, with five sacks in 17 snaps. When the defense knows a pass is coming, this line can't hold up. That shows in an 0-4 record built on one-score losses.

trend.note: His pass EPA has been negative every week: -5.6, -0.6, -6.4, then a season-low -8.0 at Seattle. That last game came with four sacks, two interceptions and a lost fumble, and the line injuries piled up during it.

nextGame.headline: Denver's soft run defense and missing corners open the door
nextGame.body:
Denver's defense fits the parts of Herbert's game that are working:
- It ranks 26th against short passes, exactly where he has been efficient.
- It ranks 7th against deep throws, where he has been broken, so the matchup rewards the quick game he can still run.
- It is 31st against the run, which suits a Harbaugh offense already passing 9 points below expectation.
- It allows 17.1 PPR and 263 yards per game to quarterbacks, both bottom-half ranks.

Expect a run-first plan with high-percentage throws rather than a shootout.

Availability cuts both ways. Pat Surtain II is doubtful and expected to miss about two weeks, and Riley Moss is questionable with a rib injury. Losing both starting corners would weaken Denver's coverage badly. On the Chargers' side, Slater is out, Alt is questionable with a neck injury, and Awosika and Penning are uncertain. Denver's 6th-ranked hit rate could still reach him even though its sack rate sits 20th. McConkey's foot matters most among the pass catchers: without his +0.629 EPA per target, the target share shifts toward Johnston and Gadsden, who have been flat or negative.

keyMatchups.title: Chargers run game vs a 31st-ranked front
keyMatchups.body: Denver is allowing positive EPA per rush, 31st in the league, and gives up explosive runs at a 26th-ranked rate. A run-heavy plan keeps Herbert out of the long-yardage downs that have produced most of his sacks and turnovers.

keyMatchups.title: Quick game vs a leaky short zone
keyMatchups.body: Denver ranks 26th in EPA allowed on short throws, and Herbert's 0-9 yard passing is his best area. If Surtain and Moss both sit, the underneath windows get bigger still.

keyMatchups.title: Patched tackles vs Denver's hits
keyMatchups.body: Denver ranks 6th in hit rate, and the Chargers are now without Slater and possibly Alt. Pressure could again drive the drive-killing sacks and hurried deep throws.

nextGame.watch: Whether Alt plays, and whether the plan leans on runs and short throws instead of asking Herbert to hold the ball for downfield shots behind backup tackles.

restOfSeason.body:
The interception rate (5%) and the deep-ball collapse should both improve. Neither fits a career built on positive efficiency, and the samples are small: 17 deep attempts and six interceptions. The protection problem is real and has a timeline, with Slater not due back until about November 1. Until then, expect efficiency closer to league average than to his 2024 form.

Volume will stay modest, with about 30 attempts a game in an offense that passes well below expectation. That caps his yardage even as the efficiency recovers. The red-zone touchdown rate will cool. Scrambling should hold up as a steady yardage floor: he ran for 498 yards last year, and pressure keeps forcing him out of the pocket.
swingFactors: Whether Harbaugh keeps the pass rate low in one-score games

bets.reason: The market has swung from Chargers -8.5 and -6.5 at home to +3.5 at home after an 0-3-1 ATS start. Denver's defense ranks 23rd in EPA and 31st against the run and may be missing both starting corners. The Chargers' 11th-ranked defense keeps games close; all four losses were by 12 or fewer.
The Chargers' offense ranks 31st in EPA and has scored 14, 14, 16 and 23. Three of their four games went under. A run-heavy plan against a soft run defense shortens the game.

He scrambles on 9% of dropbacks behind a line that ranks last in hit rate and is losing its left tackle, and Denver gets hits at a 6th-ranked rate. He ran for 40 yards in the most pressure-filled game so far, and for 498 yards last season.

All six interceptions came on 10-plus-yard throws, and Denver ranks 7th against the deep ball while sitting 26th against short passes. That should push the plan toward the turnover-free quick game. A 5% interception rate is also well beyond his career norms.

confidence.note: Four-game sample, a strong career baseline, and an offensive line in flux week to week.
